🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009 to June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s global corporate banking portal. Its treasury operations ran through separate regional systems, while Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform needed custom engineering for the bank’s payment, security, and workflow requirements. Corporate treasurers faced fragmented payment systems and separate local logins. Client administrators spent days manually configuring user permissions.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working through where WebSeries’ native capabilities ended and bank-specific development was required.

He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and tax payment modules, including NACHA file validation, payment integrity verification through Message Authentication Codes, and payment-type-specific permissions. Contextual help explained wire fields, tax codes, and FX requirements directly within payment workflows. He also delivered the centralized gateway for message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**.

For client administrators, Matt replaced individual permission changes with role-based profiles and bulk changes across users, accounts, and products from a single screen. Entitlement management dropped from **days to minutes**. He also led payments data migration without disruption to live payment operations, preserving client configurations, entitlements, transaction histories, and compliance traceability.

For the regional rollout, he translated jurisdiction-specific requirements into data visibility and access controls, sequencing launches around regulatory readiness. He owned on-call and critical incident response, coordinating root-cause analysis and live status updates.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, consolidating regional systems into a unified portal serving **135,000+ clients across 180+ countries**. Corporate treasurers gained a single entry point for payments across regions, with global cash reporting and single sign-on across treasury functions.

🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. Many teams he inherited were “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His focus was to remove those barriers: make intent explicit, create psychological safety so people could speak honestly, and push decisions to the people closest to the work.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, that meant coaching teams to think clearly, not just execute tasks. He used transparency, direct feedback, and open communication, alongside automation, continuous delivery, and quality-first engineering practices. Teams accelerated delivery **4x** once they embraced lean product and modern engineering practices. The change did not happen overnight.

His “permit to fail” learning environment addressed a specific problem: teams avoided risks because they feared blame. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems, emphasized lessons rather than finger-pointing, and supported lean, low-stakes experiments with structured hypotheses and controlled iterations. Teams applied lessons to subsequent sprints, preventing recurrence of identified failure patterns and shortening project timelines.

Matt also built balanced teams: Product + Engineering + Design together. Rather than handing work between role silos, engineers, product managers, and UX architects shared accountability for outcomes. He embedded pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, and knowledge-sharing sessions, and gave teams room to change their own workflows.

Those teams reduced handoffs and project delays and achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.

🐾 Here’s what Matt has built, changed, and delivered.

Matt’s work centers on Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement. He builds new capabilities: products, platforms, and teams that last beyond the engagement. His career has taken him from software engineer to Director, then to building the organization that builds those systems.

At **Accenture**, clients were struggling with slow development cycles, siloed teams, and legacy systems. They needed to change how they built software, not just deliver another project. Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0 to 150+ practitioners**, with full P&L accountability. He brought product managers, designers, and engineers together in balanced teams, replacing handoffs with pair programming, test-driven development, and automated pipelines.

That included changing how people learned. New hires often lacked hands-on cloud-native experience. Matt paired junior practitioners with experienced mentors and used an “I do, we do, you do” progression from guided to independent delivery. The talent program recorded near-zero attrition in its first **2 years**.

When delivery went wrong, he addressed it directly. At **Norfolk Southern**, defects were rising despite near-complete test coverage. Matt took ownership in front of the client and account leadership, audited the code and tests, and found tests written after the code alongside vague backlog stories. He rebuilt the backlog with testable stories and brought in experts to coach alongside engineers. The client stopped finding defects the dashboard could not see.

Across the CIC, teams achieved **4X faster velocity** and zero-defect deployments through TDD and automated pipelines. At **JP Morgan**, teams outpaced peer velocity within the first **2 sprints**. The centers delivered **30+ product engagements** across **15+ enterprise clients**, generating **\$100M+ in repeat business** through delivery excellence and customer relationships.
